title: भाषा योजनाको उद्देश्य, कार्य र आवश्यकता
authors: तिमल्सेना Timalsena, शिव प्रसाद Shiva Prasad
nepali: भाषाको विकास, संरक्षण, संवर्धन र स्तर निर्धारणका सम्बन्धमा भाषा नीति अनुसार आधिकारिक रूपमा तय गरिने कार्यान्वयनको खाकालाई भाषा योजना भनिन्छ । यस्तो योजना कार्यमूलक र प्रायोगिक खालको हुनु पर्दछ । जसले भाषिक नीतिमा अघि सारिएका विषयलाई कार्यान्वयनको बाटोमा लैजाने गर्दछ । भाषा योजना मूलतः भाषाको शुद्धीकरण, पुनरुत्थान, सुधार, मानकीकरण, विस्तार, कोशको आधुनिकीकरण, पारिभाषिक शब्दावलीको प्रयोग, शैलीगत सरलीकरण, अन्तरभाषिक सञ्चार तथा सहायक कोडको निर्माण गर्ने उद्देश्यले तयार पारिएको हुन्छ । भाषा योजनाले मूलतः भाषिक व्यवस्थापन, भाषाको संरक्षण, विकास र संवर्धन, भाषिक जीवन्तता तथा सामाजिक सद्भाव र राष्ट्रियताको भावको जागरण आदि कार्य गर्ने गर्दछ । यसरी भाषालाई विस्तार गर्ने, भाषिक जीवन्तता कायम गर्ने, राष्ट्रिय अखण्डता कायम गर्ने, भाषालाई देश विदेशसम्म प्रचारप्रसार गर्ने आदि कार्य गर्ने भएकाले एक भाषिक वा बहुभाषिक मुलुकका लागि भाषा योजनाको निर्माण र कार्यान्वयन आवश्यक मानिन्छ । तर नेपालको सन्दर्भमा हेर्दा प्रभावकारी भाषा योजनाको निर्माण र कार्यान्वयनमा अग्रसर भएको अवस्था पाइँदैन । यिनै सन्दर्भमा यस लेखमा भाषा योजनाको परिचय दिई यसका उद्देश्य, कार्य तथा आवश्यकतालाई निरूपण गर्ने प्रयास गरिएको छ । गुणात्मक ढाँचामा संरचित यस लेखमा आवश्यक सामग्रीको सङ्कलन पुस्तकालय पद्धतिबाट विभिन्न सन्दर्भकृतिका सहायताले गरिएको छ भने तिनको सङ्गठन र प्रस्तुतीकरणका लागि वर्णनात्मक र व्याख्यात्मक विधि अपनाइएको छ ।
american_english: The blueprint of implementation officially determined in accordance with language policy regarding the development, preservation, promotion and standardization of language is called language planning. Such a plan must be functional and practical in nature. It carries the matters set out in language policy along the path of implementation. Language planning is essentially prepared with the purpose of purifying, reviving, reforming, standardizing, and expanding language, modernizing dictionaries, using technical terminology, stylistic simplification, interlingual communication, and constructing auxiliary codes. Language planning essentially carries out tasks such as linguistic management, the preservation, development and promotion of language, linguistic vitality, and awakening the sentiment of social harmony and nationalism. Thus, because it performs tasks such as expanding language, maintaining linguistic vitality, maintaining national integrity, and promoting language at home and abroad, the construction and implementation of language planning is considered necessary for a monolingual or multilingual country. However, looking at Nepal's context, a state of having taken the lead in the construction and implementation of effective language planning is not found. In these very contexts, this article attempts to introduce language planning and to expound its objectives, functions and necessity. Structured in a qualitative format, the necessary material in this article has been collected through the library method with the help of various reference works, while a descriptive and interpretive method has been adopted for their organization and presentation.

informal_english: So language planning is basically the official blueprint for putting a language policy into practice, covering the development, preservation, promotion and standardization of a language. A plan like that has to be practical and actually workable. It's what takes the things a language policy puts forward and turns them into action. Basically, language planning is put together to purify, revive, reform, standardize and expand a language, modernize dictionaries, use technical terms, simplify style, help communication between languages, and build auxiliary codes. On the whole it does jobs like managing language, preserving, developing and promoting it, keeping it alive, and stirring up a sense of social harmony and nationalism. Because it does things like expanding a language, keeping it alive, holding national integrity together, and promoting the language at home and abroad, putting together and carrying out a language plan is seen as necessary for any country, whether it has one language or many. But looking at Nepal, there's really no sign of anyone having taken the lead in building and putting into practice an effective language plan. Against that backdrop, this article tries to introduce language planning and spell out its aims, functions and why it's needed. The article is structured qualitatively: the material was gathered through the library method with help from various reference works, and a descriptive and interpretive method was used to organize and present it.
